storyboard.title: Apollo 11: First Steps on the Moon

scenes.heading: Apollo 11: First Steps on the Moon
scenes.subheading: How did Apollo 11 land humans on the Moon?
scenes.narration: On July 16, 1969, a Saturn V rocket lifted three astronauts toward the Moon for the first crewed landing mission.
Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins rode the command module toward lunar orbit.
Three days later, Armstrong and Aldrin entered the lunar module Eagle and began their descent to the surface.
Eagle touched down at Tranquility Base in the Sea of Tranquility on July 20, 1969.

scenes.text: That's one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind.
scenes.narration: Armstrong stepped onto the Moon at 10:56 pm EDT and called it a giant leap for mankind.

scenes.label: Delay before Aldrin joined Armstrong
scenes.narration: Aldrin joined him 20 minutes later and they spent over two hours outside the module.
They set up experiments, collected volcanic samples, and planted a flag within 100 meters of Eagle.

scenes.label: Orbit altitude
scenes.narration: Collins waited alone in Columbia, circling the Moon at an altitude of 97 to 121 kilometers.
On July 21, Eagle's ascent stage launched at 17:54 UTC and rejoined Collins in lunar orbit.
The crew left lunar orbit the next day and splashed down in the Pacific on July 24, 1969.
